findings.title: GUI single scans are filed with CORRECTED pixels labelled raw; the full-resolution view, Save As, Save all and Export flat-field them a second time
findings.evidence: session.py:1441 `image, meta = self._scanner.scan(... keep_raw=True,)`; 1456 `self._file(seq, 0, image, meta, job.notes, tuple(job.tags) + ("gui",), mono=..., mono_channel=...)` (no raw_image). _prescan at 1415 does `raw_image = getattr(self._scanner, "last_pixels_raw", None)`. FrameWriter: `entry = library.save(job["image"] if raw_image is None else raw_image, ...)`. library.save: `"corrections_applied": list(corrections or [])`. library.corrected: `image, report = apply_shading(image, record["reference"], record["ccd_mask"])`. tests/test_session.py:229-236 checks only raw.bin.gz, not scan.tif.
findings.description: DirectScanner.scan returns the flat-fielded image and keeps the raw one in last_pixels_raw. ScanSession._scan never hands the raw pixels to _file, so every GUI single scan's scan.tif is the corrected picture while its record says nothing is baked in and shading.npz sits beside it.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator scans at 1800 dpi in the window. scan.tif is corrected; _load_full and Save As/Save all/roll Export call library.corrected, which divides by the reference again, over-gaining edge columns and clipping; `make reconstruct` reports every GUI scan as 'decode CHANGED', hiding real regressions.
findings.recommendation: In _scan pass raw_image=getattr(self._scanner, 'last_pixels_raw', None). Make library.save/FrameWriter refuse (or label corrections=['shading']) when meta['shading'] is set but no raw pixels were supplied. Add a session test that scan.tif equals the scanner's raw pixels; repair existing entries with `tools/library.py migrate-raw --write` (their raw.bin.gz is correct).

findings.title: Roll export joins library entries by film.frame and cannot tell a walk's prescan from the frame scan; the winner is arbitrary glob order
findings.evidence: Walk prescans are filed with `replace(job.notes, frame=job.notes.frame or f"{name}-{number:02d}")` (session.py:1827) and frames with the same `frame=job.notes.frame or f"{name}-{number:02d}"` (1881). roll_entry_index: `for record_path in root.glob("*/scan.json"): ... roll, _, number = frame.rpartition("-") ... out.setdefault(roll, {})[int(number)] = record_path.parent` -- no tag/kind/dpi filter, last one wins. roll_exports builds one export item per entry in summary["entries"].
findings.description: A GUI walk followed by a scan of the same roll leaves two entries (a 300 dpi 8-bit prescan and the full-resolution frame) per frame number under the same key, plus one more per rescan. Path.glob returns directory order, so which entry export re-corrects is arbitrary; walked-but-never-scanned frames are listed as exportable too. Rolls sharing a name (a second walk with the same date name) also share keys.
findings.failure_scenario: Walk a strip, scan frames 3 and 5, then Export the roll: frame 3 may be written from its 431-px prescan entry, frames 1,2,4,6... are exported as prescans although they were never scanned, and nothing in the dialog says so.
findings.recommendation: Record the library entry id per frame in roll.json/survey.json and join on it; at minimum filter out entries tagged 'prescan' and pick by roll folder, dpi and newest created, and use one frame-label format for GUI and CLI.

findings.title: scan_roll.py --no-shading (and scan.py --no-shading --auto-exposure) forces a lazy calibration inside the first pass -- the path the tool itself records as stalling the device
findings.evidence: scan_roll.py calibrate(): `scanner.ensure_shading(ref_path, reuse=args.reuse, skip=args.no_shading)`; args.no_shading is read nowhere else. scan_roll() has no shading parameter; prescan() always passes `shading=True` and the frame `self.scan(...)` call omits shading (default True). scan(): `if self._shading is None or needed > ...: self._log("calibrating before scanning ..."); self.calibrate_shading()`. scan_roll.py:436-440 comment: 'that lazy calibration stalls: `bulk read of 16384 bytes failed after 0 bytes: LIBUSB_ERROR_PIPE`, right after the shading descriptor, and the device stops answering'. auto_exposure's probes also call scan() with shading defaulted to True.
findings.description: --no-shading does not produce raw frames on a roll at all; it only removes the explicit calibration, so the first prescan calibrates lazily mid-roll. The same happens for tools/scan.py --no-shading --auto-exposure (the metering probe calibrates) and for probe scripts that meter before calibrating (tools/byte14_probe.py).
findings.failure_scenario: `scan_roll.py --no-shading --dry-run` seeks, skips calibration, then the first prescan starts calibrate_shading inside scan(); by the tool's own measurement this stalled with LIBUSB_ERROR_PIPE and the scanner needed a power cycle.
findings.recommendation: Thread shading through scan_roll/prescan (and auto_exposure probes) so --no-shading means raw passes, or refuse --no-shading for rolls; make lazy calibration inside scan() an error unless explicitly allowed, so every calibration goes through ensure_shading.

findings.title: Calibration bytes are thrown away; stored shading.npz cannot be recomputed with newer code
findings.evidence: `def calibrate_shading(self, resolution: int = 3600, timeout: float = 300.0, keep_data: bool = False)`; `data = b"".join(collected)` / `self._shading = calculate_shading(data, width)` / `"data": data if keep_data else None`. ensure_shading: `result = self.calibrate_shading()`. The calibration-info block is only logged: `self._log(f"calibration info: {info[:12].hex(' ')}")`.
findings.description: The reference is the output of calculate_shading's level split (split_ratio 5.0, widest gap) and averaging. The calibration lines, shading descriptor, 128-byte calibration info, the calibration pass's own mask and gain readbacks are never stored, so every entry holds today's derived reference instead of the bytes it came from.
findings.failure_scenario: An improved dark/light split or outlier rejection cannot be applied to any existing entry, and a suspected split artefact in a column cannot be audited.
findings.recommendation: Keep the calibration bytes once per calibration (e.g. library/calibrations/<sha256>.bin.gz with descriptor, info block, mask, readbacks, time) and reference that id from every entry; let library.corrected optionally rebuild the reference.
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/library.py:21-26 '`raw.bin.gz` is the ground truth and everything else is derived from it'

findings.title: Entries do not record which calibration produced their reference, or that it was reused from the cache
findings.evidence: ensure_shading reuse branch returns `{"action": "loaded", ...}` which only reaches a log/print. library.save calibration block: `"shading", "ccd_mask", "pixels_per_line", "light_mean": [round(reference.mean[c], 1) ...], "report", "skipped"` -- no calibration time, id, source path or 'reused' flag.
findings.description: The GUI's 'Use the cached one' and scan.py/scan_roll.py --reuse load a reference from any earlier power-on; the resulting entries are indistinguishable from freshly calibrated ones, and entries sharing one calibration cannot be grouped.
findings.failure_scenario: A week-old cached reference is reused; months later a column artefact shows up in those scans and nothing in the library says they were corrected with another day's sensor state.
findings.recommendation: Give each reference a calibration id (hash + measured_at + measured/loaded) stored in the npz and in scan.json calibration.

findings.title: Roll frames and bracket passes lose their metering evidence and are recorded as commanded (exposure_metered=False)
findings.evidence: scan_roll: `scales = self.auto_exposure(target=exposure_target, infrared=infrared, film=film)` then `image, meta = self.scan(..., exposure_scale=scales, ...)` (auto_exposure not passed). scan(): `"exposure_metered": bool(auto_exposure),` and `if auto_exposure and self.last_metering is not None: meta["metering"] = self.last_metering`. scan_bracket: `scales = self.auto_exposure(film=film, infrared=infrared)` then scan(exposure_scale=pass_scale).
findings.description: Metering outside scan() on the roll (the default meter='each') and bracket paths never reaches meta, so the per-probe levels/targets/limits exist nowhere durable and every frame claims its exposure was asked for.
findings.failure_scenario: A 38-frame colour-negative roll: no entry has scan.metering; BLUE_RGBI_HEADROOM cannot be checked from ordinary work; signature treats metered scales as commands.
findings.recommendation: Attach meta['metering']=self.last_metering and a metered flag for frames whose scales came from auto_exposure (reference the first frame's metering for meter='once').
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/direct.py:2026-2028 'What each round measured is left on last_metering, and scan files it with the entry'

findings.title: Debug filing attaches a previous pass's raw bytes to any pass that did not ask keep_raw
findings.evidence: read_planes: `if keep_raw: self.last_raw = blob; self.last_raw_layout = {...}` and nothing clears last_raw at the start of scan(). _debug_capture: `record = self.capture_record()` / `raw = record.get("raw")` -> spooled as this pass's raw. byte14_probe ladder uses `keep_raw=True`, its final pass `keep_raw=False, byte14=None` at the same resolution and frame, and the probe refuses to run without RPS7200_DEBUG. library.save does no layout-vs-image check.
findings.description: A keep_raw=False pass under debug filing is filed with the last keep_raw=True pass's bytes and layout (every auto_exposure probe is one), or with none. When shapes match nothing detects it.
findings.failure_scenario: RPS7200_DEBUG=1 tools/byte14_probe.py: the final default pass is filed with the last ladder pass's raw.bin.gz; reconstruct reports 'decode CHANGED'; `migrate-raw --write` then overwrites the correct scan.tif with the other pass's decode.
findings.recommendation: Clear last_raw/last_raw_layout at the top of scan(); force keep_raw when self.debug; validate layout against the image in library.save; make migrate-raw check the stored image is a correction of the decode before rewriting.

findings.title: `tools/library.py duplicates --delete` deletes scans of different photographs when film notes are empty
findings.evidence: signature returns `(stock, frame, subject, resolution_dpi, channels, frame window, depth, film, protocol_revision, commanded, fast_infrared)` -- no time, transport position or content. tools/library.py: `if args.delete: shutil.rmtree(path)`. GUI single scans/prescans use _notes() (empty unless typed); debug entries use `FilmNotes(notes="captured with RPS7200_DEBUG on")`.
findings.description: Every GUI prescan/single scan and every debug entry with the same settings and empty stock/frame/subject shares one signature; walk prescans of two strips walked under the same roll name also collide; a typed 'frame' field collapses a whole roll.
findings.failure_scenario: Ten GUI prescans of ten different frames are reported redundant and `--delete` removes nine without confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Treat entries as duplicates only with non-empty stock+frame and matching transport/roll position, add a content check, confirm and move to a trash folder instead of rmtree.

findings.title: approved.json is written to a different folder than the roll it belongs to
findings.evidence: _write_approved: `name = _safe(self.fields["roll"].get().strip())` / `folder = Path(self.session.rolls) / name`. _roll: `name = job.name or time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")` / `out = ... self.rolls / name`. `_safe("")` returns "roll". The GUI keeps `self._sheet_roll = getattr(self.session, "last_roll_dir", None)` but _write_approved does not use it; open_roll does not set fields["roll"].
findings.description: The one roll file the code calls non-derivable is filed under a recomputed, sanitised name while the roll writes under the raw name or today's date.
findings.failure_scenario: Empty roll name: walk and roll go to rolls/2026-09-24/, approved.json to rolls/roll/approved.json (overwritten by the next unnamed commission); reopening 2026-09-24 shows no decisions. 'Gold 200' splits into rolls/Gold 200/ and rolls/Gold-200/.
findings.recommendation: Write approved.json into _sheet_roll/last_roll_dir (or let _roll write it into `out`), set the roll-name field in open_roll, sanitise once in session._roll.
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/session.py:1147-1152 '...can ask rather than recompute the same name and drift out of step with it'

findings.title: tools/scan_roll.py overwrites roll.json when a roll is resumed
findings.evidence: `manifest = {"roll": roll_name, ..., "held": held_note, "frames": []}`; checkpoint(): `manifest_path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, ...))`; no existing manifest read. GUI: `"frames": list(earlier.get("frames") or [])`.
findings.description: The CLI resume path replaces earlier frame records (registration, exposure, entry paths, done flags) with only the new run's frames.
findings.failure_scenario: A 24-frame roll dies at 11; `--start-at 12` rewrites roll.json with frames 12-24; the GUI then offers 1-11 as unscanned.
findings.recommendation: Reuse session._roll's merge or route the CLI through ScanSession.

findings.title: CLI dry-run walks file nothing in the library
findings.evidence: `pre = out / f"prescan{number:02d}.tif"` / `tiff.write(str(pre), frame.prescan)`; frame.raw_prescan and s.capture_record() unused. GUI dry run: `self._file(seq, number, rf.prescan, ..., raw_image=rf.raw_prescan, path=surveyed, ...)`.
findings.description: CLI walk prescans exist only as corrected TIFFs; no raw bytes, raw pixels, reference or mask. GUI and CLI diverge.
findings.failure_scenario: Deleting a CLI walk's roll folder (the GUI says everything but approved.json is in the library) loses every prescan irrecoverably.
findings.recommendation: Submit each dry-run prescan to FrameWriter with raw_image, prescan_meta and capture_record(), as session._roll does.
findings.doc_reference: tools/gui.py:2487-2490 'Everything in a roll folder is re-derivable from the library **except `approved.json`**'

findings.title: A frame's prescan is stored corrected and unlabelled; arrival and verification prescans of held frames are never kept
findings.evidence: `prescan=rf.prescan,` while rf.raw_prescan is not passed; library.save `tiff.write(str(path / "prescan.tif"), prescan)`; held branch `prescan_image = fix["prescan"]` with no prescan_before; prescan_before is only filed on dry runs and with file_entry=False.
findings.description: prescan.tif in a frame entry is corrected with no raw bytes or mask and nothing says so; the arrival prescan and intermediate hold passes are discarded.
findings.failure_scenario: A held frame lands badly and there is no stored picture of where it arrived or of the hold's intermediate moves.
findings.recommendation: File every prescan/verification pass as its own raw entry linked by id, or store raw_prescan + mask + bytes and label prescan corrections; set prescan_before in the held branch.

findings.title: Roll and hold-loop prescans record film 'negative' whatever the roll's film
findings.evidence: `def prescan(..., film: str = FILM_NEGATIVE)`; scan_roll: `self.prescan(resolution=prescan_resolution, keep_raw=keep_raw)`.
findings.description: prescan_meta says film='negative' on B&W/slide rolls, and GUI walk entries are filed with scan.film='negative'; signature and demo selection key on it.
findings.failure_scenario: A B&W walk's prescan entries claim colour negative.
findings.recommendation: Pass film through scan_roll -> prescan, _hold_to_approved and _aim_frame.

findings.title: 7200 dpi scan.tif is realigned but the record does not say so; reconstruct and migrate-raw can never validate it
findings.evidence: `if resolution == self.NATIVE_COLUMN_STAGGER_DPI: ... image = self._realign_native_column_stagger(image)` (log only) then `raw_pixels = image`; reconstruct uses `DirectScanner.decode_index(raw, params, ...)` without realignment -> `decode CHANGED: now {image.shape}, stored {stored.shape}`.
findings.description: Reachable only with shading=False (scan.py --no-shading, API) since shading=True refuses 7200 dpi before the pass. Such scan.tif is decode + realignment, no field records it, reconstruct flags it forever, migrate-raw fails it, and ScanSession's lines guard would drop its raw bytes.
findings.failure_scenario: Every `scan.py --dpi 7200 --no-shading` entry shows '!' in `make reconstruct`; a real 7200 dpi decode regression is indistinguishable.
findings.recommendation: Record the realignment in meta and apply it in one shared decode used by scan(), reconstruct and decode_raw, or store the plain decode and realign downstream.

findings.title: ScanSession guard drops the raw bytes of a short read, the case where they matter most
findings.evidence: `actual = {"lines": shape[0], ...}` vs `layout["lines"]` (= params.lines); on disagreement `capture = dict(capture, raw=None, raw_path=None, raw_layout=None)` -- reference and ccd_mask kept. read_planes: `except EndOfData: ... break`; layout also carries `lines_received`.
findings.description: A pass that ended early decodes to fewer rows than params.lines, so its genuine bytes are discarded; when bytes truly belong to another pass the guard still keeps that pass's mask. tools/scan_roll.py has no guard at all.
findings.failure_scenario: A frame truncated mid-roll is filed without raw.bin.gz; why it was short can never be diagnosed.
findings.recommendation: Compare with lines_received (or decode the bytes); drop mask/reference too when the pass cannot be matched; share one guard with the CLI.

findings.title: library.save discards inquiry, caller meta and capture time; scan() does not record protocol overrides
findings.evidence: save(..., inquiry: Any = None, ...) never uses `inquiry`; `when = datetime.now(timezone.utc)` at filing; scan block is a fixed whitelist, dropping bracket_index/ratio/passes/stops, roll_index, roll_position, demo. scan() never records byte14, slide_init_param, skip_shading or the base Settings; _debug_capture's `"captured": time.time()` is never passed on.
findings.description: Parameters needed to re-evaluate a scan are silently lost and 'created' is the filing time.
findings.failure_scenario: byte14 ladder entries do not say which byte14 each used; bracket members cannot be regrouped; roll frames do not record their transport position; the scanner firmware is unrecorded.
findings.recommendation: Store unknown meta keys under scan.extra, record inquiry, the MODE SELECT/GAIN payload bytes sent, and a captured_at taken in scan().

findings.title: GUI single scans and prescans gzip their raw bytes while the device is open and idle
findings.evidence: FrameWriter docstring: 'On this thread the write instead overlaps the next frame's scan, so the device is busy rather than idle throughout.' After _scan the worker waits in `job = self._jobs.get()` with the scanner open while FrameWriter runs library.save -> gzip.open(..., compresslevel=6).
findings.description: For a single GUI scan there is no next pass, so the device sits open and idle for the whole gzip.
findings.failure_scenario: A 3600 dpi RGBI single scan (~250 MB raw) is gzipped for tens of seconds with the device open and idle.
findings.recommendation: Spool uncompressed and gzip after close, use a store-only level while open, or measure with tools/filing_load_test.py.
findings.doc_reference: CLAUDE.md '**A single scan compresses nothing while the device is open.** ... gzipping one with the scanner open and idle preceded a wedge once.'

findings.title: Manifests and entry records are written non-atomically; a corrupt roll.json is silently discarded on resume
findings.evidence: `except (OSError, ValueError): earlier = {}` then `manifest_path.write_text(...)`; library.save and migrations use write_text/tiff.write in place; settings.save uses a .part file and replace().
findings.description: A crash during a write truncates roll.json/survey.json/scan.json/scan.tif; the next GUI resume treats the manifest as empty and overwrites it.
findings.failure_scenario: Crash while roll.json is rewritten after frame 20; resume writes a manifest with only the new frames.
findings.recommendation: Temp file + os.replace everywhere; refuse or back up when an existing manifest cannot be parsed.

findings.title: scan_roll.py: Ctrl-C abandons the read and skips writer.finish(), losing queued frames
findings.evidence: `except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001` then `writer.finish()`; comment: 'Reached through a `finally` around the whole scanning block'. scan(): `except BaseException: self._scanning = False; raise`.
findings.description: KeyboardInterrupt is not an Exception, so it unwinds past writer.finish(); the daemon writer is killed at exit with queued frames unfiled, the manifest gets no finished/stopped, and the in-flight read is abandoned.
findings.failure_scenario: Ctrl-C mid-roll: scanner needs a power cycle and the last 1-3 frames never reach the library.
findings.recommendation: try/finally for writer.finish and the final checkpoint; a SIGINT handler that sets should_stop.
findings.doc_reference: tools/scan_roll.py:598 'Reached through a `finally` around the whole scanning block'

findings.title: A second walk into the same roll folder overwrites survey.json and the prescans
findings.evidence: Default name `time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")`; `manifest_path = out / ("survey.json" if job.dry_run else "roll.json")`, `earlier` only read `if not job.dry_run`; prescans to `out / f"prescan{number:02d}.tif"` without _unclaimed.
findings.description: Two unnamed walks in a day, or a reused name, replace the first walk; an earlier approved.json then refers to other pictures.
findings.failure_scenario: Morning strip A, afternoon strip B, both unnamed: A's survey and prescans are gone and B opens with A's approvals.
findings.recommendation: Refuse or version an existing survey, or warn in the Roll dialog.

findings.title: The roll keyboard shortcut bypasses the busy guard, and any submit clears a pending stop
findings.evidence: `"roll": self.on_roll,` while prescan/scan keys go through _confirm_then (`if self.busy: ... return`). on_roll comment: 'The button this handler is behind is disabled while busy, so this cannot race a job that is still running.' submit(): `self._stop.clear(); self._jobs.put(job)`.
findings.description: Mid-walk, the roll key opens the dialog; confirming a dry run clears survey/sheet state, restarts edge_watch and clears the Stop already requested, so the current job continues and another is queued.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator presses Stop, then the roll key by mistake: the walk does not stop, its frames vanish from the sheet, and a second walk follows.
findings.recommendation: Check self.busy in on_roll; clear _stop only when the worker takes a job (it already does in _run).

findings.title: DemoScanner runs its own roll loop that diverges from DirectScanner.scan_roll
findings.evidence: demo: `prescan, _ = self.prescan(film=film)` (prescan_resolution swallowed by **kw); `self._hold_to_approved(index, prescan, 300, held, keep_raw=False, reverse=reverse_hold,)` (no should_stop); `marks["base"] = walk.observe(index, prescan)` only in the `elif walk is not None` branch; no blank-contrast end, no metering, no except/max_failures; RollFrame without raw_image/raw_prescan/prescan_before; no meta['registration'].
findings.description: The failed-frame path, end-of-film detection, prescan dpi, metering, StripWalk with held frames and raw filing of roll frames are not exercised with no device.
findings.failure_scenario: A demo frame error ends the whole roll; demo rolls always prescan at 300 dpi whatever the sheet pinned; demo roll entries have no registration.
findings.recommendation: One roll driver parameterised by prescan/scan/advance/nudge primitives, with DemoScanner supplying only the primitives.

findings.title: Demo passes return corrected pixels without last_pixels_raw, ignore shading=False and the 7200 dpi refusal, and leave stale calibration in the capture
findings.evidence: _decode: `if reference is not None and not (record.get("calibration") or {}).get("skipped"): image, self._shading_report = apply_shading(image, reference, mask)` (ignores the pass's shading flag and corrections_applied, and re-shades a scan.tif fallback); _pair_image's prescan.tif branch `return image` without touching self._capture; no last_pixels_raw attribute; scan() has no MAX_SHADING_COLUMNS check; meta has no exposure/protocol_revision/shading_skipped.
findings.description: Through the unchanged session path demo entries get corrected pixels as raw, the source entry's raw bytes when shapes match, and a reference/mask possibly from a previous decode at another resolution; a 7200 dpi scan the scanner refuses succeeds in the demo.
findings.failure_scenario: Demo prescan after a 1800 dpi scan: the demo prescan entry carries the 1800 dpi pass's ccd_mask.bin/shading.npz, and library.corrected applies it to an already-corrected 300 dpi image.
findings.recommendation: Give DemoScanner last_pixels_raw (uncorrected decode), reset _capture every pass, apply DirectScanner's width refusal via a shared static, honour shading=False, and respect corrections_applied in _decode.
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/demo.py:15-20 '...`capture_record` can hand the session genuine bytes to file. An entry the demo files reconstructs like any other.'

findings.title: Demo scan ignores the simulated film position; backlash constant retyped
findings.evidence: prescan: `self._read_as_carriage(self._as_positioned(image), ONE_PASS_COLOR)`; scan: `image = self._pair_image("scan.tif", film, resolution)` then `_read_as_carriage(image, ...)` with no _as_positioned. Backlash: `swallowed = min(abs(asked), 2.2 * 0.1057)`.
findings.description: After a hold moves the simulated film the scan still shows the unmoved picture; 0.1057 retypes protocol.MM_PER_UNIT.
findings.failure_scenario: Demo roll with an approved offset: the delivered frame is not re-centred although the log says it was held.
findings.recommendation: Apply _as_positioned (scaled to the scan dpi) in scan(); use protocol.MM_PER_UNIT.

findings.title: Roll folder name is used unsanitised, and only after the film has already been moved
findings.evidence: `seek(self._scanner, first, ...)` runs first, then `name = job.name or time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")` / `out = Path(job.out) if job.out else self.rolls / name` / `out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`; name comes from `self.fields["roll"].get().strip()`.
findings.description: A roll name with '/', '..' or Windows-illegal characters writes outside rolls/ or fails mkdir after the seek has moved the film, while approved.json goes to the _safe() name.
findings.failure_scenario: Name 'a:b' on Windows: film is rewound/advanced, then the job fails on mkdir.
findings.recommendation: Sanitise the name with _safe before seek, in one place for both GUI and CLI.

findings.title: verify reports deliberately raw scans as 'correction was asked for'
findings.evidence: `why = cal.get("skipped")` / `(f" -- correction was asked for: {why}" if why else "")` fires for SHADING_SKIPPED_EXPLICIT too.
findings.description: verify does not distinguish explicit shading=False from a shortfall.
findings.failure_scenario: `make verify` after `scan.py --no-shading` prints '... correction was asked for: shading=False (explicit)'.
findings.recommendation: Compare against SHADING_SKIPPED_EXPLICIT as corrected() does.
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/library.py:360-362 '`verify` already draws that line and calls the other one "a thing that went wrong"'

findings.title: The comparison files do not exercise the driver's correction path
findings.evidence: `raw = tiff.read(scan_path)` (default scans/negatives/state_1800dpi.tif), `corrected = destripe(raw, defects, margin=12, dilate=5)`; no library entry, raw bytes, shading.npz or apply_shading.
findings.description: 2_corrected.tif is a flat-based destripe of an arbitrary TIFF, so a regression in decode/apply_shading would not show.
findings.failure_scenario: A change breaks apply_shading; the regenerated files look unchanged and are sent as evidence.
findings.recommendation: Build 1/2/3 from a library entry: decode_raw, library.corrected, invert.
findings.doc_reference: CLAUDE.md 'Regenerate the three comparison files after any significant change to the scan or correction path'

findings.title: scan_roll.py --approved does not un-orient GUI walk prescans
findings.evidence: CLI: `frames = [(number, tiff.read(str(path))) for number, path, _ in walked_prescans(...)]` used as Approved.reference. GUI read_survey: `turn = int(manifest.get("rotation") or 0)` ... `image=preview.unorient(image, turn, mirrored)`.
findings.description: GUI walks store prescanNN.tif oriented by the session rotation/flip; the CLI proposes positions and correlates unrotated fresh prescans against rotated references.
findings.failure_scenario: A strip walked in the window with 'rotate 180' then commissioned with `--approved`: proposals are mirrored and holds go the wrong way or abstain.
findings.recommendation: Apply preview.unorient with the manifest's rotation/flipped in hold_from_walk.

findings.title: GUI roll export cannot find CLI-scanned roll entries (film.frame format differs)
findings.evidence: CLI: `frame=f"{roll_name}/{number:02d}"`; GUI: `frame=job.notes.frame or f"{name}-{number:02d}"`; roll_entry_index: `roll, _, number = frame.rpartition("-")` / `if not roll or not number.isdigit(): continue`.
findings.description: The two writers use different join strings, and a typed frame field breaks the GUI one too.
findings.failure_scenario: Export of a CLI-scanned roll says no frame has a library entry.
findings.recommendation: Join on entry ids recorded in roll.json (the CLI already records them) and use one label format.

findings.title: --look-only without --demo drives the real scanner while the window says there is no film
findings.evidence: `no_film=args.look_only` reaches only the DemoScanner constructor; without --demo, ScanSession's default DirectScanner refuses nothing.
findings.description: With a real scanner nothing refuses, so the controls move film and scan.
findings.failure_scenario: `gui.py --look-only --open-roll X` with the scanner attached: 'Scan chosen' seeks, meters and scans for real.
findings.recommendation: Reject --look-only without --demo or make ScanSession refuse transport jobs when set.

findings.title: README describes reversal-by-prescan turning that the code no longer does
findings.evidence: _note_reversal: `if _read_known(meta): ... return meta` -- a pass whose line tags gave a direction is never turned.
findings.description: README presents picture comparison against the prescan as the mechanism; the code decides from line tags and only logs a disagreement.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator expects a mismatched frame to be turned automatically; it is only logged.
findings.recommendation: Update the README.
findings.doc_reference: README.md:352-358 'A pass that comes back the wrong way up is turned to match its prescan ...'

findings.title: Transport-distance documentation disagrees with the code and with itself
findings.evidence: MM_PER_UNIT = 0.1057, COMMAND_UNITS = 1.84 (param 1 -> 2.84 units); units_for_param docstring: 'a command pays the ramp first, so `param 1` travels 2.57'. CLI --nudge and approved.json offset_mm are in millimetres.
findings.description: README states the old 0.1662 mm ramp; CLAUDE.md gives ~2.6 and 2.84 for param 1 and 344.5 vs 345.2 for the aperture; protocol.py's own docstring says 2.57; CLAUDE.md prohibits millimetres while storage is in mm.
findings.failure_scenario: A move is checked against README's 0.1662 mm or the 2.57 docstring and appears wrong.
findings.recommendation: Align README/CLAUDE.md/docstrings with protocol.py; decide whether stored offsets move to units.
findings.doc_reference: README.md:555-556 '`0.1057 × param + 0.1662` mm'; rps7200/protocol.py units_for_param docstring '`param 1` travels 2.57'; CLAUDE.md '`param 1` (~2.6 units)' vs '2.84'

findings.title: auto_exposure comment says SET GAIN OFFSET readback persists and compounds, contradicting the measured protocol notes
findings.evidence: direct.py:2064-2066 ':meth:`scan` multiplies whatever the device currently holds, and SET GAIN OFFSET persists, so re-reading it each round would compound the scales.' docs/protocol.md: '**`READ GAIN/OFFSET` is a fixed reference, not a readback.** ... exposure cannot compound'. direct.py:3632 comment in the same file says the read 'is a fixed reference'.
findings.description: Two comments in direct.py give opposite models of the device; the metering tests fake the echoing model. No wrong pixels follow today because scan_roll writes the baseline back, but the code's own reasoning is inconsistent.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer 'fixes' compounding that does not exist (as docs/whole-roll-plan.md records happened once).
findings.recommendation: Make the auto_exposure comment match the measured behaviour and keep one statement of it.

findings.title: 'File every scan' is not true of the tools or the window: metering probes and hold passes are never filed, even with RPS7200_DEBUG=1
findings.evidence: `DirectScanner(verbose=self.verbose, debug=False)`; `DirectScanner(verbose=args.verbose, debug=False)`; `self.debug = (os.environ.get(...) ... if debug is None else bool(debug))`. auto_exposure: 'CLAUDE.md's rule is "file every scan, with its raw bytes" ... keep_raw=True' yet nothing files the probe.
findings.description: Metering probes, hold-loop verification prescans and held frames' arrival prescans are discarded by the GUI and both CLI tools; the env var cannot change it.
findings.failure_scenario: A 38-frame metered roll leaves ~100 probe passes and every hold verification nowhere.
findings.recommendation: File probe and verification passes through FrameWriter (tagged probe/hold) when debug is on, or let the env var override.
findings.doc_reference: CLAUDE.md '**File every scan in the library, with its raw bytes.**'

findings.title: Debug spool is unrecoverable after a hard kill
findings.evidence: _debug_capture writes only `np.save(image_path, image)` and `raw_path.write_bytes(raw)`; meta, raw_layout, reference and ccd_mask go to `self._debug_pending` in memory; filing only in close() -> _debug_flush.
findings.description: A killed/crashed process never reaches close(); orphaned .npy/.bin files carry no meta, layout or reference and there is no recovery command.
findings.failure_scenario: A probe killed at the 10-minute harness limit loses every pass as library entries.
findings.recommendation: Write a JSON sidecar, shading npz and mask per spooled item and add a recover-spool command.

findings.title: scan.py --bracket silently ignores a single-value --exposure-scale
findings.evidence: `exposure_scale = parts[0] if len(parts) == 1 else parts`; bracket passes `exposure_scale=(list(exposure_scale) if isinstance(exposure_scale, list) else None)` and `auto_exposure=args.auto_exposure and not args.exposure_scale` -> scan_bracket `scales = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]`.
findings.description: The fixed exposure is dropped without a message.
findings.failure_scenario: `scan.py --bracket 5 --exposure-scale 2` brackets around x1.
findings.recommendation: Pass [x]*3 for a scalar.

findings.title: 7200 dpi is offered but always refused, and a roll only refuses per frame after prescan, metering and holds
findings.evidence: `self._int(self.v_dpi, "Scan dpi", 25, 7200)`; scan(): `if needed > self.MAX_SHADING_COLUMNS: raise ShadingUnavailable(...)`; scan_roll checks film/infrared up front but not width and catches ShadingUnavailable per frame.
findings.description: A 7200 dpi roll moves film and spends prescan/metering/hold time on each frame before failing up to max_failures.
findings.failure_scenario: Three frames of film movement and metering are spent before the roll gives up.
findings.recommendation: Refuse up front in scan_roll and in the dialogs, or drop 7200 from the list.

findings.title: No checksums for shading.npz, ccd_mask.bin or prescan.tif
findings.evidence: Only image.sha256 and raw.sha256 are recorded; verify only checks existence of the calibration files.
findings.description: Corruption of the reference or mask, which decide every corrected pixel, is undetectable.
findings.failure_scenario: A bit flip in shading.npz changes every future export; verify says intact.
findings.recommendation: Record and verify sha256 for every file.

findings.title: Calibrate button starts a calibration without asking whether film is loaded
findings.evidence: `self.session.submit(Calibrate(mode=mode or self.v_shading.get(), reference=self.session.reference))` with no confirmation.
findings.description: Calibrating an empty transport preceded a wedge per the project notes; the button does not ask.
findings.failure_scenario: Calibration right after power-on with the strip out.
findings.recommendation: Ask before a measured calibration.

findings.title: Library, calibration cache and roll paths are relative to the current directory
findings.evidence: `DEFAULT_ROOT = Path("library")`; `ScanSession(root="library", reference="calibration/shading.npz", rolls="rolls")`; `home = DEMO_ROOT if args.demo else Path(".")`.
findings.description: Launching from another directory silently starts a new library/cache/rolls there; `--demo --library library` files demo entries into the real library (meta['demo'] is not whitelisted).
findings.failure_scenario: `cd tools && uv run python gui.py` files into tools/library/, invisible to `make reconstruct`.
findings.recommendation: Resolve defaults against a configured data root; record demo provenance and refuse demo filing into a non-demo library.

findings.title: Quitting mid-roll waits for the whole roll and every queued job
findings.evidence: on_close: 'Quitting waits for it to finish' then `self.session.shutdown()` which only queues None; no request_stop.
findings.description: The window stays until the whole roll (hours) finishes.
findings.failure_scenario: Close 3 frames into a 38-frame roll expecting it to stop after the pass.
findings.recommendation: Offer 'stop after this frame and quit'.

findings.title: Layering: library depends on direct, with a lazy import cycle back
findings.evidence: library: `from .direct import SHADING_SKIPPED_EXPLICIT, DirectScanner, ScanParameters`; direct._debug_flush: `from . import library`; demo: `from .session import estimate_seconds`.
findings.description: The offline data layer reaches the decode through the device module, which is also why the 7200 realignment inside scan() is invisible to reconstruct.
findings.recommendation: Move decode_index/realignment/SHADING_SKIPPED_EXPLICIT into a decode module shared by direct, library and demo.
